identificationModule.briefTitle: The Combination of Teriflunomide and Danazol for Steroid-resistant/Relapse Immune Thrombocytopenia
identificationModule.officialTitle: A Multicenter, Open-label, Randomized, Controlled, Phase 2 Trial Comparing the Efficacy and Safety of Teriflunomide Plus Danazol in Patients With Steroid-resistant/Relapse ITP

descriptionModule.briefSummary: To compare the efficacy and safety of teriflunomide plus danazol versus danazol in patients with steroid-resistant/relapse ITP
descriptionModule.detailedDescription: This is a prospective, multicenter, randomized, controlled trial of 124 adult patients with steroid-resistant/relapse ITP in China. Patients were randomized to receive either experimental teriflunomide plus danazol or active comparator danazol monotherapy. Treatment was discontinued if very severe or life-threatening adverse events developed or at the patient's request.

designInfo.interventionModelDescription: Patients were randomly assigned at a 1:1 ratio to receive teriflunomide plus danazol or danazol. Each group requires 62 patients (considering a 10% drop-off).

armGroups.label: Teriflunomide plus danazol
armGroups.description: Oral teriflunomide was given at a starting dose of 7 mg once daily and danazol was given at a dose of 200mg twice daily for 24 weeks. Treatment was discontinued if very severe or life-threatening adverse events developed or at the patient's request.

armGroups.label: Danazol
armGroups.description: Danazol was given at a dose of 200 mg twice a day for 24 weeks. Treatment was discontinued if very severe or life-threatening adverse events developed or at the patient's request.

interventions.name: Teriflunomide
interventions.description: Starting dose of 7 mg once daily. Dose adjustments are made throughout the study based on individual platelet counts.

primaryOutcomes.description: Platelet count over 30,000/μL and at least a 2-fold increase of the baseline count in the absence of bleeding and rescue therapy for at least four of the six visits between weeks 19 and 24.
primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: From the start of study treatment (Day 1) to the end of week 24

secondaryOutcomes.description: Complete response (CR) was defined as platelet count over 100,000/μL and absence of bleeding. Response (R) was defined as platelet count over 30,000/μL and at least a 2-fold increase of the baseline count and absence of bleeding.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: From the start of study treatment (Day 1) to the end of week 24

secondaryOutcomes.description: The time from treatment initiation to achieve a CR or a R.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: From the start of study treatment (Day 1) to the end of week 24

secondaryOutcomes.description: The time from the achievement of a complete response or a partial response to the loss of response.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: From the start of study treatment (Day 1) to the end of week 24

secondaryOutcomes.description: The number of participants with achievement of CR or R at 4 weeks.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: From the start of study treatment (Day 1) up to week 4 of treatment

secondaryOutcomes.description: Clinically significant bleeding was assessed using the World Health Organization (WHO) bleeding scale.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: From the start of study treatment (Day 1) to the end of week 24

secondaryOutcomes.description: Adverse events (AEs) were reported and graded according to the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE), version 5.0.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: From the start of study treatment (Day 1) to the end of week 24

secondaryOutcomes.description: ITP-PAQ was used to assess the Health-Related Quality of Life (HRQoL) before and after treatment.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: From the start of study treatment (Day 1) to the end of week 24
